reason: This passage from Genesis 27 depicts familial deception and internal conflict within a household—specifically Jacob deceiving his father Isaac (with his mother Rebekah's assistance) to obtain the patriarchal blessing intended for Esau. The antagonism present is between family members (Jacob vs. Isaac through fraud; Esau vs. Jacob/Isaac after the deception is discovered), not between regular people and their leader. There is no portrayal of a general population being antagonistic toward a leader figure.
